To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose SCAN, a new framework for discovering hierarchical compositional concepts from visual data and that SCAN can be applied to a variety of tasks, such as concept generation, concept manipulation, concept recombination, concept discovery, concept classification, and concept completion.

we propose a novel framework for learning hierarchical visual concepts through symbol association, that we demonstrate its efficacy on a wide range of visual concept learning and imagination tasks, and that we show that it can learn from very little supervision.

(1) SCAN learns a hierarchy of compositional visual concepts through fast symbol associations, (2) these concepts are grounded in disentangled and interpretable visual features, and (3) SCAN is capable of generating new visual concepts through symbolic manipulation of its learned visual hierarchy
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how to learn abstract, hierarchical, compositional, and multimodal visual concepts from data, and how to use such concepts to imagine and generate novel data.
the question of how to learn a hierarchical, compositional and disentangled visual representation of the world through purely unsupervised experiences.
the question of how to learn and manipulate abstract visual concepts in a way that is interpretable to humans and generalizes beyond the distribution of training data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SCAN is a novel approach for learning hierarchical and compositional concepts in the visual domain that can be recombined and manipulated through symbolic instructions.
SCAN is a framework for learning visual concepts in an unsupervized manner and can generate new concepts through recombination of learnt visual concepts.
SCAN is a novel framework for learning hierarchical compositional visual concepts that can be recombined to imagine novel visual concepts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a new framework for concept learning in images that is capable of learning a diverse and rich set of visual concepts in an unsupervized way and allows for the manipulation of these visual concepts through symbolic language.
we have proposed a framework to learn visual concepts that are compositional and hierarchically organized, and that can be recombined to imagine new visual concepts through symbol manipulation.
we have developed an unsupervised learning algorithm for visual concepts that is capable of learning a large set of concepts from a small number of examples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SCAN can learn a rich set of visual abstractions through a simple and fast symbol association mechanism.
SCAN can learn to associate visual concepts with symbols through a few pairings and can then generate new visual concepts by recombining these learnt concepts through symbolic instructions.

SCAN is able to learn a set of visual concepts that is both rich enough for diverse image generation and hierarchical enough for compositional concept manipulation, all without any supervision or prior assumptions on the form of symbol representation.
